findings.finding: Every current DEV gold world has TRAIN support. Both languages contain 72 distinct TRAIN and 72 DEV gold worlds out of 432 ontology combinations.
findings.limit: This concerns the existing corpus only; it is not complete coverage of all ontology combinations or real-world language.

findings.finding: Selected study 75 heads have 11 binary and 9 joint-field TRAIN errors, versus 16 binary and 1,344 joint-field DEV errors. All 11 TRAIN binary errors have correct argmax for every field.
findings.limit: TRAIN fit is not held-out accuracy; categorical correctness does not ensure the fixed served probability crosses its selected threshold.

findings.finding: Of 1,344 DEV joint errors, 1,155 include formal UNCERTAIN→AFFIRMED collapse: 578 Romanian and 577 Ukrainian.
findings.limit: This is an exposed DEV diagnosis, not independent validation.

findings.finding: Within controlled_composition_v8, all 356 Romanian and 317 Ukrainian UNCERTAIN TRAIN rows have a literal negation before the first quote and zero assertion errors. All 579 Romanian and 579 Ukrainian matching DEV rows lack that literal marker; 578/577 are wrong.
findings.limit: The descriptor ignores wording after the first quote and is not a semantic scope label. This association does not establish causality.

findings.finding: Across all TRAIN sources, quoted UNCERTAIN examples without pre-quote negation do exist: 279 Romanian and 291 Ukrainian.
findings.limit: Do not claim positive uncertainty is globally absent from TRAIN.

next_intervention_hypothesis: A prospective TRAIN-only intervention should vary uncertainty wording and quote scope more independently of assertion class, including non-negating uncertainty and affirmed claims containing negation. Reuse only TRAIN payloads or newly authored cores; keep exposed DEV text/families out of fitting, retain a matched control, and audit language/label quality. More copies of the same operator templates would not test this hypothesis.
prior_related_experiments: Assertion/query studies 22–24, 30 and 33 already failed qualification; do not repeat them unchanged or describe this diagnosis as a novel algorithm.
